definitions.explanation: Fighting techniques and combat methods, encompassing both traditional Japanese martial disciplines and martial arts more broadly. Emphasizes the practical techniques of fighting.

examples.japanese: {武術|ぶじゅつ}の{稽古|けいこ}をする。
{彼|かれ}は{幼|おさな}い{頃|ころ}から{武術|ぶじゅつ}を{学|まな}んでいる。
examples.english: He has been studying martial arts since he was young.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{武術|ぶじゅつ}は{海外|かいがい}でも{高|たか}い{人気|にんき}を{集|あつ}めており、{多|おお}くの{外国人|がいこくじん}が{学|まな}びに{来|く}る。
examples.english: Traditional Japanese martial arts are highly popular overseas, and many foreigners come to study them.

notes:
SIMILAR WORDS:
{武道|ぶどう} emphasizes the spiritual and philosophical 'way' ({道|みち}) of martial training (e.g., {柔道|じゅうどう}, {剣道|けんどう}). {武術|ぶじゅつ} emphasizes practical fighting techniques ({術|じゅつ} = technique). {武芸|ぶげい} emphasizes martial skills as a cultured accomplishment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {武術|ぶじゅつ}の{稽古|けいこ}: martial arts practice
- {武術|ぶじゅつ}を{習|なら}う: to learn martial arts
- {武術|ぶじゅつ}{大会|たいかい}: martial arts tournament
- {古|こ}{武術|ぶじゅつ}: classical martial arts (kōbujutsu)

cross_references.label: martial arts, combat sports, fighting sports
